newsitem.title: USA: Texaco hires ad agency to help reach Hispanics.
newsitem.headline: Texaco hires ad agency to help reach Hispanics.

text.p: Texaco Inc., the centre of last year's high-profile race discrimination case, said Thursday it hired a Texas-based advertising agency to help reach Hispanics.

The company selected, KJS Marketing Communications, generates annual billings of more than $18 million and clients include Anheuser-Busch Cos. Inc., Columbia Healthcare Corp. and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.
Texaco's latest move comes a month after it tapped minority-owned UniWorld Group Inc. to help expansion into the black marketplace.

The moves are part of efforts by Texaco to improve its minority programmes following a scandal last year in which top executives were heard on tape making allegedly biased remarks about blacks in the company.
The scandal led to settlement of a racial bias suit for $176 million and threats of a consumer boycott by civil rights activists if the company did not boost employment and advancement of minorities.
The activists also demanded that Texaco increase its purchasing from minority-owned suppliers.
"Today's announcement is consistent with Texaco's plans to broaden its base of vendors and suppliers of services with additional women-and minority-owned firms," Texaco said in a statement Thursday.

"The KJS team has extensive experience in both the general markets and the Hispanic market, which will be critical in helping Texaco to create a consistent message and image in all segments of the marketplace," the statement added.
Texaco's stock fell $1.625 to $100.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
